answer: In this PoA design, each identity must complete a continuous chain of modular squarings, with every result depending on the previous one; a Wesolowski proof lets others verify the work efficiently. GPUs can run separate chains, but cannot compress one chain’s sequential delay, so simulating many clones requires many time-bound computations rather than free parallel identities. The grove of clones therefore faces a physical bottleneck, not a tide of instant identities, and each thread must wait for its own chain to finish.
